title: Gender-Specific Differences in the Management of Patients with Neuromuscular Diseases Receiving Non-Invasive Ventilation (NIV) – A Retrospective Single-Center Data Analysis
summary: This study aims to explore whether there are differences between men and women who require non-invasive ventilation due to a neuromuscular disease. The focus is on examining whether ventilator settings vary by gender, whether men and women differ in how well they adhere to the therapy, and whether their well-being and quality of life differ. The findings are intended to help tailor treatment more effectively to individual needs and ultimately improve overall care.

interventions.name:
Retrospective analysis
• Collection of demographic and clinical baseline data
• Analysis of capillary blood gas values
• Evaluation of extracted NIV device data
• Assessment of quality of life based on documented SRI questionnaires

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Patients with a confirmed diagnosis of a neuromuscular disease
• Chronic respiratory failure type II with established NIV therapy
• Ongoing NIV therapy for a minimum duration of 3 months
• Complete data sets available in the hospital’s documentation system CCP/KISS
Exclusion criteria:
• Age < 18 years
• Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
• Incomplete or missing data sets in the CCP/KISS documentation system
• Patients with a primary lung disease other than COPD (e.g., pulmonary fibrosis, bronchial asthma)
• Patients with acute exacerbations at the time of initial NIV initiation
